dataSources: `index=edge-hub-health` sourcetype=edge_hub, `index=edge-hub-logs` sourcetype=splunk_edge_hub_log connection_event Collected via Universal Forwarder (Splunkbase 617) modular input or scripted poll into the index named in the SPL.
app: Splunk Edge Hub (health monitoring), Splunk OT Intelligence — Universal Forwarder (Splunkbase 617)
spl:
index=edge-hub-health sourcetype=edge_hub gateway_name=*
| stats latest(connection_status) as status, latest(response_time_ms) as response_time,
        count(eval(error_code!=0)) as error_count by gateway_name, host
| eval gateway_health=case(
    status="CONNECTED" AND response_time < 1000 AND error_count < 5, "HEALTHY",
    status="CONNECTED" AND response_time >= 1000, "SLOW",
    status="DISCONNECTED" OR error_count > 10, "DEGRADED",
    1=1, "UNKNOWN")
description: Tracks OPC-UA/Modbus/MQTT gateway uptime and connection quality to prevent silent data loss. Searches `index=edge-hub-health` with sourcetype `edge_hub` for UC-14.3.34, aggregating `count` by `gateway_name` over `the scheduled window`. Alerts when grouped results cross `response_time` < 1000 in the saved search. Gives Operations operators a repeatable signal for 'Protocol Gateway Health & Connectivity Monitoring' without manual log review.
value: Early 'Protocol Gateway Health & Connectivity Monitoring' detection reduces operational risk and delayed incident response by giving Operations operators a Splunk-native signal before manual triage or audit channels surface the issue.
implementation: Edge Hub continuously monitors OPC-UA (port 4840), Modbus TCP (port 502), and MQTT broker (port 1883) connectivity every 15 seconds. Log connection attempts + response times to edge-hub-health index (sourcetype=edge_hub). Track error codes (authentication failures, timeouts, handshake errors). Store 100K health events locally. If gateway disconnects, LED ring turns red. Resume transmission via local SQLite backlog (FIFO) when connectivity restored. Configure alert thresholds: downtime > 1 minute = critical, response time > 2s = warning.
visualization: Gateway uptime timeline, response time histogram, error rate trend.
dataModelAcceleration: Not applicable (no CIM or Operational_Telemetry data model in this SPL).
knownFalsePositives:
1. **Maintenance window on `edge-hub-health`** — Planned work for 'Protocol Gateway Health & Connectivity Monitoring' shifts `count` over `span=1h` while `gateway_name` remains in-scope for UC-14.3.34. Cross-check CMDB CHG.

2. **Batch `count` on `edge_hub`** — Scheduled automation elevates `host` without crossing `response_time` < 1000. Compare `_time` minute against the job schedule.

3. **Synthetic probe on `gateway_name`** — Health checks in `edge-hub-health` populate the same fields the SPL groups on. Exclude monitoring-tagged assets before paging.

4. **Onboarding burst for `edge_hub`** — First 48h baseline for `gateway_name` is unstable; window via `ops_exception_register.csv`.

**Suppression mechanism:** `ops_exception_register.csv` keyed on `gateway_name`, `exception_reason`, `valid_until`.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Install and configure the required add-on or app: Splunk Edge Hub (health monitoring), Splunk OT Intelligence.
• Ensure the following data sources are available: `index=edge-hub-health` sourcetype=edge_hub, `index=edge-hub-logs` sourcetype=splunk_edge_hub_log connection_event.
• For app installation, inputs.conf, and Splunk directory layout, see the Implementation guide: docs/implementation-guide.md

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Edge Hub continuously monitors OPC-UA (port 4840), Modbus TCP (port 502), and MQTT broker (port 1883) connectivity every 15 seconds. Log connection attempts + response times to edge-hub-health index (sourcetype=edge_hub). Track error codes (authentication failures, timeouts, handshake errors). Store 100K health events locally. If gateway disconnects, LED ring turns red. Resume transmission via local SQLite backlog (FIFO) when connectivity restored. Configure alert thresholds: downtime > 1 minute…

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
Run the following SPL in Search (then save as report or alert; adjust time range and threshold as needed):

```spl
index=edge-hub-health sourcetype=edge_hub gateway_name=*
| stats latest(connection_status) as status, latest(response_time_ms) as response_time,
        count(eval(error_code!=0)) as error_count by gateway_name, host
| eval gateway_health=case(
    status="CONNECTED" AND response_time < 1000 AND error_count < 5, "HEALTHY",
    status="CONNECTED" AND response_time >= 1000, "SLOW",
    status="DISCONNECTED" OR error_count > 10, "DEGRADED",
    1=1, "UNKNOWN")
```

Understanding this SPL

**Protocol Gateway Health & Connectivity Monitoring** — Tracks OPC-UA/Modbus/MQTT gateway uptime and connection quality to prevent silent data loss.

Documented **Data sources**: `index=edge-hub-health` sourcetype=edge_hub, `index=edge-hub-logs` sourcetype=splunk_edge_hub_log connection_event. **App/TA** (typical add-on context): Splunk Edge Hub (health monitoring), Splunk OT Intelligence. The SPL below should target the same indexes and sourcetypes you configured for that feed—rename `index=` / `sourcetype=` if your deployment differs.

The first pipeline stage scopes events using **index**: edge-hub-health; **sourcetype**: edge_hub. That sourcetype matches what this use case lists under Data sources.

**Pipeline walkthrough**

• Scopes the data: index=edge-hub-health, sourcetype=edge_hub. Cross-check against **Data sources** above so indexes and sourcetypes match your ingestion.
• `stats` rolls up events into metrics; results are split **by gateway_name, host** so each row reflects one combination of those dimensions.
• `eval` defines or adjusts **gateway_health** — often to normalize units, derive a ratio, or prepare for thresholds.


Step 3 — Validate
Confirm metric or event volume in the time range, then compare trends and device status to the Splunk Edge Hub admin UI or the mobile app for the same devices. Verify metric names, hosts, and time skew.

Step 4 — Operationalize
Add the search to a dashboard or set up alert actions (email, webhook, PagerDuty, etc.) as required. Document the use case in your runbook and assign an owner. Consider visualizations: Gateway uptime timeline, response time histogram, error rate trend.
